# Education Policies: NEP 2020, NCF-SE 2023, NIPUN Bharat, PM SHRI, Samagra Shiksha

This is the core "educational policies" block of the syllabus. UPSC asks dates, numbers, full forms, who-launched-what, and the exact structure of each scheme. Read the tables twice.

## 1. NEP 2020 (राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति 2020): how it came about

- India's **third** national education policy, after **NPE 1968** and **NPE 1986** (modified **1992**). It replaced a 34-year-old policy.
- Two committees prepared it: the **T.S.R. Subramanian Committee** (report **2016**) and then the drafting committee chaired by **Dr K. Kasturirangan** (former ISRO chief), constituted **June 2017**, which submitted the draft on **31 May 2019**.
- The **Union Cabinet approved NEP 2020 on 29 July 2020**. At the same meeting the **Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD) was renamed the Ministry of Education (शिक्षा मंत्रालय)**.
- NEP is a **policy, not a law**. Education is on the **Concurrent List (Entry 25, List III)**, so States implement it through their own schemes, with Samagra Shiksha and PM SHRI as the main central funding channels.
- Five foundational pillars: **Access, Equity, Quality, Affordability, Accountability** (पहुँच, समता, गुणवत्ता, वहनीयता, जवाबदेही).
- The document has **27 chapters in four parts**: Part I School Education (Ch. 1–8), Part II Higher Education (Ch. 9–19), Part III Other key areas (professional education, adult education, Indian languages, technology, online education), Part IV Making it happen (CABE, financing, implementation).

| Part I chapter | Theme |
|---|---|
| 1 | Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) |
| 2 | Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN) |
| 3 | Curtailing dropout, universal access |
| 4 | Curriculum and pedagogy in schools |
| 5 | Teachers |
| 6 | Equitable and inclusive education |
| 7 | School complexes/clusters |
| 8 | Standard-setting and accreditation (SSSA, SQAAF) |

## 2. NEP 2020: the school-education provisions UPSC asks

### The 5+3+3+4 structure (replacing 10+2)

| Stage (चरण) | Ages | Grades | Pedagogy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Foundational (बुनियादी) | 3–8 | 3 years Anganwadi/Balvatika + Grades 1–2 | Play and activity based |
| Preparatory (प्रारंभिक) | 8–11 | Grades 3–5 | Play, discovery, activity, light textbooks |
| Middle (मध्य) | 11–14 | Grades 6–8 | Subject teachers, experiential; vocational exposure |
| Secondary (माध्यमिक) | 14–18 | Grades 9–12 (two phases: 9–10, 11–12) | Multidisciplinary, choice, semesters |

Note the two 3-year blocks: the Foundational stage is **5 years** because it adds three pre-school years to Grades 1–2.

### Key targets and numbers

| Target | Figure |
|---|---|
| Public investment in education | **6% of GDP** (first recommended by the Kothari Commission 1964–66) |
| Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) in school, pre-school to secondary | **100% by 2030** |
| GER in higher education | **50% by 2035** (from **26.3% in 2018**) |
| Out-of-school children to be brought back | about **2 crore** |
| Universal FLN | NEP said by **2025**; the mission (NIPUN) set **2026-27** |
| Vocational exposure | at least **50% of learners by 2025** |
| Minimum teacher qualification | **4-year integrated B.Ed. by 2030** |
| Continuous professional development (CPD) | at least **50 hours per year** per teacher |
| Pupil-teacher ratio | under **30:1** at each school; under **25:1** where SEDGs are many |
| National Professional Standards for Teachers (NPST) | to be developed by NCTE (target 2022) |

### Language, curriculum and assessment

- **Medium of instruction**: home language / mother tongue / local language **at least till Grade 5, preferably till Grade 8 and beyond** (मातृभाषा में शिक्षण).
- **Three-language formula** continues with flexibility; **no language will be imposed**; at least **two of the three languages must be native to India**. Sanskrit offered at all levels; foreign languages at secondary level; **Indian Sign Language** to be standardised.
- **Curriculum reduced to core essentials**; no hard separation between arts and sciences, curricular and extra-curricular, vocational and academic.
- **Vocational education from Grade 6**, with internships and a **10-day bagless period** in Grades 6–8. Coding from middle stage.
- **Board exams** (Grades 10, 12) continue but become "easier", test core competencies, and may be taken **up to two times a year** (one main, one improvement). **2026 was CBSE's first year of two Class 10 board exams**: the main exam ran 17 Feb–11 Mar and the optional second (improvement) exam ran 15–21 May. The better of the two scores counts.
- **Census examinations in Grades 3, 5 and 8** by the State to track learning, in addition to boards.
- **360-degree Holistic Progress Card (समग्र प्रगति पत्रक)** replacing marks-only report cards; self, peer and teacher assessment.
- **PARAKH** (Performance Assessment, Review and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development) is the National Assessment Centre proposed by NEP; **set up in NCERT in February 2023**. It conducted the **PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan on 4 December 2024** in Classes **3, 6 and 9**, which replaced the earlier NAS (NAS 2021 was in Classes 3, 5, 8, 10). It also prepared the **SQAAF** (titled School Quality Assessment and Assurance Framework; the NEP text calls it the School Quality Assessment and Accreditation Framework) and the **Holistic Progress Cards**.
- Early childhood: universal quality ECCE by **2030**; a **National Curricular and Pedagogical Framework for ECCE** by NCERT (this became **NCF-FS 2022**); one-year **Balvatika** before Grade 1; **3-month school preparation module** (this became **Vidya Pravesh**).

### Equity, governance and teachers

- **SEDGs** (Socio-Economically Disadvantaged Groups) is the umbrella term; **Gender Inclusion Fund**; **Special Education Zones**; KGBVs extended to Grade 12.
- **School complexes/clusters** (an idea from the Kothari Commission) to share resources; **Bal Bhavans**; schools as **Samajik Chetna Kendras**.
- **State School Standards Authority (SSSA)** as an independent regulator in each State; **SCERT** to frame the school quality framework.
- Teachers: TET extended to all stages; merit-based recruitment; halt to frequent transfers; **National Mission for Mentoring**; teacher education moved to multidisciplinary institutions; the 4-year **Integrated Teacher Education Programme (ITEP)** began in 2023-24.
- **Supreme Court (Sept 2025, reviews dismissed May 2026)**: TET is mandatory for in-service teachers to continue and be promoted; deadline **31 August 2028**.

### Higher education in one glance (short, but asked)

- **HECI** (Higher Education Commission of India) is NEP's proposed single regulator with **four verticals**: NHERC (regulation), NAC (accreditation), HEGC (grants), GEC (standards); medical and legal education excluded. The **Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan (VBSA) Bill, 2025** was introduced in the Lok Sabha on **15 Dec 2025** and referred to a **Joint Parliamentary Committee** on 16 Dec 2025. It would create a single regulator replacing **UGC, AICTE and NCTE** through **three councils**: Viniyaman Parishad (regulation), Gunvatta Parishad (accreditation) and Manak Parishad (standards). Unlike HECI, it has **no grant-giving arm**. It was still pending with the JPC in October 2026.
- **4-year undergraduate degree with multiple entry and exit**; **Academic Bank of Credits (ABC)**; **M.Phil discontinued**; **National Research Foundation** (enacted as **Anusandhan NRF Act 2023**); **National Educational Technology Forum (NETF)**; **National Credit Framework (NCrF) 2023**; common entrance tests by NTA.
- Adult education: **ULLAS / Nav Bharat Saksharta Karyakram (2022-27)** for non-literates aged **15+**; a State is "fully literate" at **95%** adult literacy. Mizoram was first (2025); Sikkim (5th) and Uttarakhand (6th) were declared in 2026; **Ladakh** was the first fully literate UT.

## 3. NCF-SE 2023 (स्कूली शिक्षा के लिए राष्ट्रीय पाठ्यचर्या की रूपरेखा 2023)

### The four NCFs mandated by NEP

| Framework | Status |
|---|---|
| NCF for Foundational Stage (NCF-FS) | Released **20 October 2022** (ages 3–8). First NCF under NEP |
| NCF for School Education (NCF-SE) | Released **23 August 2023** (full school stage) |
| NCF for Teacher Education (NCFTE) | NEP assigns it to **NCTE in consultation with NCERT** |
| NCF for Adult Education (NCFAE) | NEP assigns it to a new **NCERT constituent body for adult education** |

- Earlier NCFs: **1975, 1988, 2000, 2005** (NCF 2005 under Prof. **Yash Pal**). NCF-SE 2023 is the first full revision in 18 years.
- Developed by **NCERT** under the **National Steering Committee chaired by Dr K. Kasturirangan** (constituted Sept 2021), with State-level inputs collected via the **NCF mobile app survey** and District Consultations.
- **Jadui Pitara (जादुई पिटारा)**, the play-based learning-teaching material box for ages 3–8, was launched on **20 February 2023** under NCF-FS.

### Core design of NCF-SE

- Follows **5+3+3+4** and the stage-wise pedagogy above; uses a chain **Aims → Curricular Goals → Competencies → Learning Outcomes**.
- Foundational stage: development of the whole child through the **Panchakosha (पंचकोश)** view: physical (शारीरिक), life-energy (प्राणिक), mental/emotional (मानसिक), intellectual (बौद्धिक), spiritual (चैतसिक/आध्यात्मिक).
- **No formal written exams in the Foundational stage**; assessment through observation and portfolios; written tests from Grade 3 onwards.
- Languages are labelled **R1, R2, R3** (not "first/second language"). **Grades 9–10: three languages, at least two native to India. Grades 11–12: two languages, at least one native to India.**
- **Grades 9–10**: eight curricular areas (Humanities incl. languages; Mathematics and Computational Thinking; Vocational Education; Physical Education and Well-being; Arts; Social Science; Science; Interdisciplinary Areas).
- **Grades 11–12**: **semester system**, choice-based; students take two languages and **four subjects from at least two of three subject groups**, removing the rigid science/commerce/humanities streams.
- **Board exams at least twice a year**, with the better score counting; the long-term goal is on-demand board exams. Both Grade 10 and 12 boards stay.
- **Vocational education** across stages, framed as three forms of work: with life forms (agriculture, animal husbandry), with materials and machines, and in human services.
- Values and **rootedness in India** (Indian knowledge systems), environmental education, and lighter school bags.
- **New NCERT textbooks**: Grades 1–2 in 2023-24 (e.g. *Mridang*, *Sarangi*, *Joyful Mathematics*); Grades 3 and 6 in 2024-25 (*Ganita Prakash*, *Curiosity*, *Exploring Society: India and Beyond*, *Poorvi*); Grades 4, 5, 7, 8 in 2025-26; Grade 9 in 2026-27 (*Ganita Manjari*, *Understanding Society*).
- Current affairs link: **AI and Computational Thinking from Class 3 from 2026-27**, framed by CBSE and NCERT under NCF-SE; the NCERT Class 8 social science chapter on the judiciary was withdrawn after Supreme Court suo motu action (closed 1 Sept 2026).

## 4. NIPUN Bharat (निपुण भारत)

- **Full form: National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy** (समझ और संख्या ज्ञान के साथ पढ़ने में दक्षता के लिए राष्ट्रीय पहल).
- **Launched 5 July 2021** by the then Education Minister **Ramesh Pokhriyal 'Nishank'** (Dharmendra Pradhan took charge on 7 July 2021). It implements NEP's National Mission on FLN and runs **under Samagra Shiksha**, not as a separate scheme.
- **Goal**: every child attains **foundational literacy and numeracy (बुनियादी साक्षरता एवं संख्या ज्ञान) by the end of Grade 3 by 2026-27**. Coverage: ages **3–9**, Balvatika to Grade 3.
- **Three developmental goals**: (1) children maintain good health and well-being; (2) children become effective communicators; (3) children become involved learners and connect with their immediate environment.
- **Lakshya Soochi (लक्ष्य सूची)**: stage-wise targets from Balvatika to Grade 3; the Grade 3 reading target is reading **at least 60 words per minute with comprehension**.
- **Five-tier implementation mechanism**: National, State, District, Block/Cluster, School. Teachers and head of school (HoS) are responsible for school-level tracking.
- Related tools: **Vidya Pravesh (विद्या प्रवेश)**, a **3-month (12-week) play-based school preparation module for Grade 1**; **Balvatika** (one-year pre-school class in primary schools); **NISHTHA 3.0 (FLN)**, with **12 online courses** on DIKSHA for pre-primary to Grade 5 teachers, launched Sept 2021; the **Foundational Learning Study (FLS) 2022** by NCERT (Grade 3, March 2022) that set benchmarks; and the **NIPUN Bharat Stakeholders' Roles and Responsibilities** document.
- NISHTHA (National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement) itself began on **21 August 2019** (NISHTHA 1.0, elementary, 18 modules); 2.0 for secondary (2021), 3.0 FLN (2021), 4.0 ECCE.
- Delhi angle: the Directorate of Education ran **Mission Buniyaad (2018)** for FLN; from 2025 the government reported new programmes (NEEEV, Science of Living, Rashtraneeti) replacing earlier flagship initiatives.

## 5. PM SHRI (पीएम श्री: प्रधानमंत्री स्कूल्स फॉर राइजिंग इंडिया)

- Announced by the Prime Minister on **Teachers' Day, 5 September 2022**; **approved by the Union Cabinet on 7 September 2022**.
- A **Centrally Sponsored Scheme** to develop **more than 14,500 schools** as **exemplar NEP 2020 schools**, across all tiers: Central (KVs, JNVs), State/UT and local-body schools.
- **Period: 2022-23 to 2026-27** (five years). **Total cost Rs 27,360 crore**, of which the **Central share is Rs 18,128 crore**. About **18 lakh students** are expected to benefit directly.
- **Fund sharing**: 60:40 Centre:State; 90:10 for NE and Himalayan States; 100% Central for UTs without legislature.
- **Selection by Challenge Mode** on the PM SHRI portal in rounds: the State/UT first signs an **MoU** to implement NEP in full; eligible schools are drawn from **UDISE+** against minimum benchmarks (own pucca building, toilets, drinking water, electricity, barrier-free access); schools self-apply, are physically verified, and an expert committee approves the list. **Maximum two schools per block / urban local body** (one elementary, one secondary/senior secondary). On **29 July 2023** (NEP's third anniversary) the Prime Minister released the **first instalment of funds to 6,207 PM SHRI schools**.
- **Six pillars of quality** (used in the School Quality Assessment Framework, SQAF): (1) curriculum, pedagogy and assessment; (2) access and infrastructure; (3) human resources and school leadership; (4) inclusive practices and gender equity; (5) management, monitoring and governance; (6) beneficiary satisfaction.
- Features: **green school** components (solar, LED, nutrition gardens, waste management, rainwater harvesting, plastic-free), ICT and smart classrooms, labs including ATLs, vocational interventions with local industry, **Vidya Samiksha Kendra** data linkage, mentoring, and school-level **Principal's Action Plan**.
- Delhi angle: Delhi stayed out of PM SHRI under the earlier government. The present government launched its own **CM SHRI schools (2025)**; **Heritage Clubs** were opened in 75 CM SHRI schools in Sept 2026, and language labs run in CM SHRI and other schools.

## 6. Samagra Shiksha (समग्र शिक्षा)

- An **integrated Centrally Sponsored Scheme** for school education from **pre-school to Class 12**, launched in **2018-19** (effective 1 April 2018) by subsuming three schemes: **Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA, 2001)**, **Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA, 2009)** and **Teacher Education (TE)**. Mid-day meal (now **PM POSHAN**) is a **separate** scheme.
- **Samagra Shiksha 2.0**: approved by Cabinet on **4 August 2021** for **2021-22 to 2025-26**, aligned with NEP 2020. Outlay **Rs 2,94,283.04 crore** (Central share **Rs 1,85,398.32 crore**). The cycle ended on **31 March 2026**; a restructured "Samagra Shiksha 3.0" was under consultation in 2026, with no confirmed Cabinet approval as of early October 2026. If asked, the approved framework remains Samagra Shiksha 2.0.
- **Fund sharing**: **60:40** for States and **UTs with legislature (Delhi, Puducherry)**; **90:10** for NE and Himalayan States and J&K; **100%** Central for UTs without legislature.
- Implemented through a **State Implementation Society (SIS)** with a **Single Nodal Agency (SNA)** bank account and PFMS; planning and monitoring via **PRABANDH** portal; school data via **UDISE+**; grading via **PGI**.
- Major components: ECCE and Balvatika; **NIPUN Bharat**; **KGBVs up to Class 12**; **Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Awasiya Vidyalayas**; inclusive education for CWSN; vocational education from Class 6; ICT and digital initiatives; **NISHTHA** training; **Rani Laxmibai Atma Raksha Prashikshan** (girls' self-defence, raised to **Rs 5,000 per school per month for 3 months**); **transport allowance Rs 6,000 per child per year**; **Vidyanjali** volunteer programme; Holistic Progress Card; bagless days.

| Composite school grant (संयुक्त विद्यालय अनुदान), per year | Enrolment |
|---|---|
| Rs 10,000 | up to 30 students |
| Rs 25,000 | 31–100 |
| Rs 50,000 | 101–250 |
| Rs 75,000 | 251–1,000 |
| Rs 1,00,000 | above 1,000 |

- **10% of the composite grant** must go to the **Swachhta Action Plan**. Library grant Rs 5,000–20,000 and sports grant **Rs 5,000 / 10,000 / 25,000** (primary / upper primary / secondary and above). CWSN support of **Rs 3,500 per child per year**.
- For a Vice Principal this is the money that reaches the school: know the slabs, the Swachhta earmark, the SMC's role in the School Development Plan, and that unspent balances and utilisation certificates flow back through PFMS.

## 7. Digital and data backbone (short recall)

| Item | Fact |
|---|---|
| DIKSHA | National teacher/student platform, launched **5 September 2017**; hosts NISHTHA |
| PM eVIDYA | **17 May 2020**; "One Class One Channel" DTH channels, radio, ISL content |
| NDEAR | National Digital Education Architecture blueprint, **29 July 2021** |
| APAAR ID | Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry, "One Nation One Student ID", linked to DigiLocker/ABC |
| UDISE+ 2025-26 | About **1.02 crore** teachers (the 1-crore mark was first crossed in UDISE+ 2024-25); about 14.67 lakh schools |
| PGI 2.0 2025-26 | 1,000-point index; Chandigarh alone in Uttam-3 (766 points, 4th straight year on top); Delhi among the next four |

## Common traps

- **Cabinet approval 29 July 2020**, not the draft date (31 May 2019) and not 2019 or 2021. Chair is **Kasturirangan**, not Subramanian (he chaired the earlier 2016 committee).
- **Preparatory = Grades 3–5 (ages 8–11)**; Foundational is **five** years because it includes three pre-school years.
- **GER 50% by 2035 is for higher education**; school GER target is 100% by 2030.
- Mother tongue "at least till Grade 5, preferably 8" — options that say "compulsory till Grade 8" are wrong.
- NEP **did not abolish board exams**; it allowed them twice a year and added census exams in Grades 3, 5, 8.
- **NIPUN launched 5 July 2021 by Ramesh Pokhriyal**, target **2026-27**, under Samagra Shiksha (not a stand-alone CSS).
- **NCF-FS 2022 came before NCF-SE 2023**; both are by NCERT under Kasturirangan's steering committee, not by CBSE or NCTE.
- NCF-SE languages: **three in 9–10, two in 11–12**; R1/R2/R3 labels.
- **PM SHRI approved 7 Sept 2022** (announced 5 Sept); **more than 14,500 schools; Rs 27,360 crore; 2022-23 to 2026-27**; KVs and JNVs are eligible; maximum two schools per block.
- Samagra Shiksha subsumes **SSA + RMSA + Teacher Education**; not mid-day meal. **2.0 approved 4 Aug 2021**, outlay **Rs 2,94,283 crore**.
- Delhi's fund-sharing is **60:40** because it is a UT **with** legislature; UTs without legislature get 100%.
- PARAKH is a **unit of NCERT (2023)**, and its 2024 survey covered Classes **3, 6, 9** (NAS 2021 covered 3, 5, 8, 10).
- HECI (NEP) has **four** verticals including grants; the VBSA Bill 2025 has **three** councils and no grant function.

## Remember for the exam

1. NEP 2020: Cabinet approval 29 July 2020; Kasturirangan draft 31 May 2019; MHRD became Ministry of Education.
2. Structure 5+3+3+4: ages 3–8, 8–11, 11–14, 14–18.
3. Targets: 6% of GDP; higher-education GER 50% by 2035; school GER 100% by 2030; 4-year B.Ed by 2030; 50 hours CPD.
4. Mother tongue till at least Grade 5, preferably Grade 8; two of three languages must be Indian.
5. Vocational from Grade 6 with 10 bagless days; census exams in Grades 3, 5, 8; boards up to twice a year.
6. PARAKH set up Feb 2023 in NCERT; Rashtriya Sarvekshan 4 Dec 2024, Classes 3, 6, 9.
7. NCF-FS released 20 Oct 2022; Jadui Pitara 20 Feb 2023; NCF-SE released 23 Aug 2023.
8. NCF-SE: Panchakosha, R1/R2/R3, three languages in 9–10 and two in 11–12, semesters in 11–12, boards twice a year.
9. NIPUN Bharat: 5 July 2021; FLN by end of Grade 3 by 2026-27; ages 3–9; five-tier mechanism; three developmental goals.
10. Vidya Pravesh: 3-month school preparation module for Grade 1; NISHTHA 3.0 FLN has 12 courses.
11. PM SHRI: Cabinet 7 Sept 2022; more than 14,500 schools; Rs 27,360 cr (Central Rs 18,128 cr); 2022-23 to 2026-27; six pillars; challenge mode; two schools per block.
12. Samagra Shiksha: 2018-19; SSA + RMSA + TE; pre-school to Class 12; 2.0 approved 4 Aug 2021, Rs 2,94,283 cr, 2021-22 to 2025-26.
13. Composite school grant Rs 10,000 to Rs 1,00,000 by enrolment; 10% for Swachhta Action Plan.
14. Fund sharing: 60:40 States and Delhi; 90:10 NE/Himalayan/J&K; 100% for UTs without legislature.
15. ULLAS 2022-27, age 15+, fully literate = 95%; HECI four verticals; VBSA Bill 2025 (three councils, replaces UGC/AICTE/NCTE) pending with JPC.
quick_facts: NEP 2020 was approved by the Union Cabinet on 29 July 2020; the drafting committee was chaired by Dr K. Kasturirangan (draft submitted 31 May 2019); MHRD was renamed Ministry of Education the same day.
NEP 2020 replaced NPE 1986 (modified 1992) and is India's third national education policy after 1968 and 1986.
5+3+3+4: Foundational ages 3–8 (3 pre-school years + Grades 1–2), Preparatory 8–11 (Grades 3–5), Middle 11–14 (Grades 6–8), Secondary 14–18 (Grades 9–12).
NEP targets: 6% of GDP on education; higher-education GER 50% by 2035 (26.3% in 2018); school GER 100% by 2030; 4-year integrated B.Ed as minimum teacher qualification by 2030; 50 hours CPD a year.
Medium of instruction in home language/mother tongue at least till Grade 5, preferably till Grade 8; three-language formula with at least two Indian languages and no language imposed.

NEP keeps board exams (up to twice a year) and adds State census exams in Grades 3, 5 and 8; PARAKH was set up in NCERT in Feb 2023 and held the Rashtriya Sarvekshan on 4 Dec 2024 in Classes 3, 6 and 9.

NCF for Foundational Stage was released on 20 Oct 2022 (ages 3–8); Jadui Pitara on 20 Feb 2023; NCF for School Education on 23 Aug 2023, all by NCERT under Kasturirangan's National Steering Committee.

NCF-SE 2023: Panchakosha development, languages labelled R1/R2/R3, three languages in Grades 9–10 (two Indian), two languages in Grades 11–12, semester system in 11–12, board exams at least twice a year.

NIPUN Bharat (National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy) was launched on 5 July 2021 by Ramesh Pokhriyal 'Nishank' under Samagra Shiksha; goal: FLN for every child by end of Grade 3 by 2026-27; covers ages 3–9.

NIPUN has three developmental goals, a Lakshya Soochi of stage-wise targets, and a five-tier mechanism (National, State, District, Block/Cluster, School); Vidya Pravesh is the 3-month school-preparation module for Grade 1; NISHTHA 3.0 (FLN) has 12 courses.

PM SHRI was announced on 5 Sept 2022 and approved by Cabinet on 7 Sept 2022: more than 14,500 exemplar schools, Rs 27,360 crore (Central share Rs 18,128 crore), 2022-23 to 2026-27, selection by challenge mode with at most two schools per block/ULB.

PM SHRI has six quality pillars: curriculum-pedagogy-assessment; access and infrastructure; human resources and leadership; inclusion and gender equity; management-monitoring-governance; beneficiary satisfaction.

Samagra Shiksha (2018-19) subsumed SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education and covers pre-school to Class 12; Samagra Shiksha 2.0 was approved on 4 Aug 2021 for 2021-22 to 2025-26 with an outlay of Rs 2,94,283 crore.
Composite school grant: Rs 10,000 (up to 30 students), 25,000 (31–100), 50,000 (101–250), 75,000 (251–1,000), 1,00,000 (above 1,000); 10% is earmarked for the Swachhta Action Plan.
Fund sharing under Samagra Shiksha and PM SHRI: 60:40 for States and UTs with legislature (Delhi), 90:10 for NE and Himalayan States, 100% Central for UTs without legislature.

mcqs.source: NEP 2020, Ministry of Education; PIB release of 29 July 2020

mcqs.q_en: Under the 5+3+3+4 structure of NEP 2020, the Preparatory Stage covers:
mcqs.q_hi: NEP 2020 की 5+3+3+4 संरचना के अंतर्गत प्रारंभिक (Preparatory) चरण में सम्मिलित हैं:
mcqs.explain_en: Foundational is ages 3–8 (three pre-school years plus Grades 1–2), Preparatory is Grades 3–5 (ages 8–11), Middle is Grades 6–8 and Secondary is Grades 9–12.
mcqs.explain_hi: बुनियादी चरण आयु 3–8 (तीन पूर्व-प्राथमिक वर्ष + कक्षा 1–2), प्रारंभिक चरण कक्षा 3–5 (आयु 8–11), मध्य चरण कक्षा 6–8 और माध्यमिक चरण कक्षा 9–12 है।

mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements about NEP 2020:
1. It aims to raise the Gross Enrolment Ratio in higher education to 50% by 2035.
2. It reaffirms public investment in education of 6% of GDP.
3. It recommends the home language or mother tongue as the medium of instruction at least till Grade 5, preferably till Grade 8.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
NEP 2020 के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. इसका लक्ष्य उच्च शिक्षा में सकल नामांकन अनुपात को 2035 तक 50% करना है।
2. यह शिक्षा पर सार्वजनिक निवेश सकल घरेलू उत्पाद के 6% करने की पुनः पुष्टि करती है।
3. यह कम से कम कक्षा 5 तक, और अधिमानतः कक्षा 8 तक, घरेलू भाषा/मातृभाषा को शिक्षण का माध्यम बनाने की अनुशंसा करती है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: All three are explicit NEP 2020 provisions: GER 50% by 2035 (from 26.3% in 2018), 6% of GDP, and mother-tongue medium at least till Grade 5, preferably Grade 8 and beyond.
mcqs.explain_hi: तीनों कथन NEP 2020 के स्पष्ट प्रावधान हैं: 2035 तक उच्च शिक्षा में GER 50% (2018 में 26.3%), GDP का 6%, और कम से कम कक्षा 5 तथा अधिमानतः कक्षा 8 तक मातृभाषा माध्यम।

mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements about NIPUN Bharat:
1. It was launched on 5 July 2021.
2. Its goal is that every child attains foundational literacy and numeracy by the end of Grade 3 by 2026-27.
3. It is a separate centrally sponsored scheme outside Samagra Shiksha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
निपुण भारत के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. इसे 5 जुलाई 2021 को प्रारंभ किया गया।
2. इसका लक्ष्य है कि 2026-27 तक प्रत्येक बच्चा कक्षा 3 के अंत तक बुनियादी साक्षरता एवं संख्या ज्ञान प्राप्त कर ले।
3. यह समग्र शिक्षा से अलग एक पृथक केंद्र प्रायोजित योजना है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: NIPUN Bharat was launched on 5 July 2021 with the Grade 3 by 2026-27 target. Statement 3 is wrong: it is implemented as a component under Samagra Shiksha, not as a separate scheme.
mcqs.explain_hi: निपुण भारत 5 जुलाई 2021 को प्रारंभ हुआ और इसका लक्ष्य 2026-27 तक कक्षा 3 के अंत तक FLN है। कथन 3 गलत है: इसे समग्र शिक्षा के घटक के रूप में लागू किया जाता है, पृथक योजना के रूप में नहीं।

mcqs.q_en: In 'NIPUN Bharat', the word NIPUN stands for:
mcqs.q_hi: 'निपुण भारत' में NIPUN का पूर्ण रूप है:
options_en: National Institute for Primary and Upper-primary Numeracy
National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy
National Integrated Programme for Universal Numeracy
National Initiative for Primary Understanding and Nutrition
options_hi: नेशनल इंस्टीट्यूट फॉर प्राइमरी एंड अपर-प्राइमरी न्यूमरेसी
नेशनल इनिशिएटिव फॉर प्रोफिशिएंसी इन रीडिंग विद अंडरस्टैंडिंग एंड न्यूमरेसी
नेशनल इंटीग्रेटेड प्रोग्राम फॉर यूनिवर्सल न्यूमरेसी
नेशनल इनिशिएटिव फॉर प्राइमरी अंडरस्टैंडिंग एंड न्यूट्रिशन
mcqs.explain_en: NIPUN is National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy, the FLN mission under NEP 2020 and Samagra Shiksha. The other expansions are invented.
mcqs.explain_hi: NIPUN का अर्थ है National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy, जो NEP 2020 और समग्र शिक्षा के अंतर्गत FLN मिशन है। अन्य विकल्प काल्पनिक हैं।

mcqs.q_en:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes:
List-I: A. NCF for Foundational Stage released; B. NCF for School Education released; C. PARAKH set up in NCERT; D. NIPUN Bharat launched
List-II: 1. 5 July 2021; 2. February 2023; 3. 20 October 2022; 4. 23 August 2023
mcqs.q_hi:
सूची-I को सूची-II से सुमेलित कीजिए और कूट से सही उत्तर चुनिए:
सूची-I: A. बुनियादी चरण के लिए NCF जारी; B. स्कूली शिक्षा के लिए NCF जारी; C. NCERT में PARAKH की स्थापना; D. निपुण भारत का शुभारंभ
सूची-II: 1. 5 जुलाई 2021; 2. फरवरी 2023; 3. 20 अक्टूबर 2022; 4. 23 अगस्त 2023
mcqs.explain_en: NCF-FS came out on 20 Oct 2022, NCF-SE on 23 Aug 2023, PARAKH was set up in Feb 2023 and NIPUN Bharat was launched on 5 July 2021. Option 1 swaps the two NCFs, the usual trap.
mcqs.explain_hi: NCF-FS 20 अक्टूबर 2022 को, NCF-SE 23 अगस्त 2023 को जारी हुई, PARAKH की स्थापना फरवरी 2023 में हुई और निपुण भारत 5 जुलाई 2021 को प्रारंभ हुआ। विकल्प 1 में दोनों NCF की तिथियाँ बदल दी गई हैं।
mcqs.source: NCERT NCF-FS 2022 and NCF-SE 2023; PARAKH (NCERT); NIPUN Bharat guidelines

mcqs.q_en:
Assertion (A): Under Samagra Shiksha, the Centre and the Government of NCT of Delhi share the cost in the ratio 60:40.
Reason (R): Delhi is a Union Territory with a Legislature, and such UTs are treated like States for fund sharing, while UTs without a Legislature get 100% Central funding.
mcqs.q_hi:
अभिकथन (A): समग्र शिक्षा के अंतर्गत केंद्र और दिल्ली राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र सरकार 60:40 के अनुपात में लागत साझा करते हैं।
कारण (R): दिल्ली विधानमंडल वाला संघ राज्यक्षेत्र है और ऐसे संघ राज्यक्षेत्रों को निधि साझाकरण में राज्यों की तरह माना जाता है, जबकि बिना विधानमंडल वाले संघ राज्यक्षेत्रों को 100% केंद्रीय वित्तपोषण मिलता है।
options_en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
options_hi: A और R दोनों सत्य हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या है
A और R दोनों सत्य हैं परंतु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है
A सत्य है परंतु R असत्य है
A असत्य है परंतु R सत्य है
mcqs.explain_en: Samagra Shiksha funding is 60:40 for States and UTs with Legislature (Delhi, Puducherry), 90:10 for NE and Himalayan States and J&K, and 100% Central for UTs without Legislature. R states exactly why Delhi is at 60:40.
mcqs.explain_hi: समग्र शिक्षा में राज्यों और विधानमंडल वाले संघ राज्यक्षेत्रों (दिल्ली, पुदुचेरी) के लिए 60:40, पूर्वोत्तर/हिमालयी राज्यों व जम्मू-कश्मीर के लिए 90:10 और बिना विधानमंडल वाले संघ राज्यक्षेत्रों के लिए 100% केंद्रीय निधि है। R, A का सही कारण बताता है।
mcqs.source: Samagra Shiksha Framework for Implementation (fund-sharing pattern); Cabinet approval of Samagra Shiksha 2.0, 4 Aug 2021

mcqs.q_en: Which of the following statements about the PM SHRI scheme is NOT correct?
mcqs.q_hi: पीएम श्री योजना के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही नहीं है?
options_en: It was approved by the Union Cabinet on 7 September 2022
Schools are selected in challenge mode, with at most two schools per block or urban local body
Only State and UT government schools are eligible; Kendriya Vidyalayas and Navodaya Vidyalayas are excluded
options_hi: इसे केंद्रीय मंत्रिमंडल ने 7 सितंबर 2022 को अनुमोदित किया
विद्यालयों का चयन चैलेंज मोड में होता है, प्रति ब्लॉक/शहरी स्थानीय निकाय अधिकतम दो विद्यालय
केवल राज्य/संघ राज्यक्षेत्र सरकार के विद्यालय पात्र हैं; केंद्रीय विद्यालय और नवोदय विद्यालय इसमें शामिल नहीं हैं
mcqs.explain_en: PM SHRI covers schools managed by the Centre (including KVs and JNVs), States/UTs and local bodies, so option 4 is wrong. The other three are correct features of the scheme (more than 14,500 schools, Rs 27,360 crore).
mcqs.explain_hi: पीएम श्री में केंद्र (केंद्रीय विद्यालय और नवोदय विद्यालय सहित), राज्यों/संघ राज्यक्षेत्रों और स्थानीय निकायों द्वारा संचालित विद्यालय शामिल हैं, अतः विकल्प 4 गलत है। अन्य तीन योजना की सही विशेषताएँ हैं (14,500 से अधिक विद्यालय, ₹27,360 करोड़)।
mcqs.source: PM SHRI Implementation and Programmatic Guidelines, Part 1; Cabinet decision 7 Sept 2022

mcqs.q_en:
Samagra Shiksha was launched in 2018-19 by subsuming which of the following?
1. Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan
2. Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan
3. Mid-Day Meal Scheme
4. Centrally Sponsored Scheme on Teacher Education
Select the correct answer using the codes:
mcqs.q_hi:
समग्र शिक्षा 2018-19 में निम्नलिखित में से किन योजनाओं को समाहित करके प्रारंभ की गई?
1. राष्ट्रीय माध्यमिक शिक्षा अभियान
2. सर्व शिक्षा अभियान
3. मध्याह्न भोजन योजना
4. शिक्षक शिक्षा की केंद्र प्रायोजित योजना
कूट से सही उत्तर चुनिए:
mcqs.explain_en: Samagra Shiksha merged SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education into one scheme from pre-school to Class 12. The mid-day meal scheme (now PM POSHAN) stayed a separate scheme.
mcqs.explain_hi: समग्र शिक्षा ने SSA, RMSA और शिक्षक शिक्षा को पूर्व-प्राथमिक से कक्षा 12 तक की एक योजना में मिलाया। मध्याह्न भोजन (अब पीएम पोषण) एक अलग योजना बनी रही।

mcqs.q_en: Under the Samagra Shiksha norms, a government school with an enrolment of 500 students is entitled to an annual composite school grant of:
mcqs.q_hi: समग्र शिक्षा मानदंडों के अंतर्गत 500 विद्यार्थियों के नामांकन वाला सरकारी विद्यालय प्रति वर्ष कितने संयुक्त विद्यालय अनुदान का पात्र है?
mcqs.explain_en: The slabs are Rs 10,000 (up to 30 students), 25,000 (31–100), 50,000 (101–250), 75,000 (251–1,000) and 1,00,000 (above 1,000). A school of 500 falls in the 251–1,000 slab. Ten percent of the grant is for the Swachhta Action Plan.
mcqs.source: Samagra Shiksha Framework for Implementation, Programmatic and Financial Norms (composite school grant)

mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements about NCF-SE 2023:
1. In Grades 9 and 10 students learn three languages, of which at least two must be native to India.
2. In Grades 11 and 12 students learn two languages, at least one of which is native to India.
3. The framework applies only to the Foundational Stage (ages 3–8).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
NCF-SE 2023 के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. कक्षा 9 और 10 में विद्यार्थी तीन भाषाएँ सीखते हैं, जिनमें से कम से कम दो भारत की मूल भाषाएँ होनी चाहिए।
2. कक्षा 11 और 12 में विद्यार्थी दो भाषाएँ सीखते हैं, जिनमें से कम से कम एक भारत की मूल भाषा होती है।
3. यह रूपरेखा केवल बुनियादी चरण (आयु 3–8) पर लागू होती है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: NCF-SE 2023 prescribes three languages in Grades 9–10 (two Indian) and two in Grades 11–12 (one Indian). Statement 3 describes NCF-FS 2022; NCF-SE covers the whole 5+3+3+4 school stage.
mcqs.explain_hi: NCF-SE 2023 कक्षा 9–10 में तीन भाषाएँ (दो भारतीय) और कक्षा 11–12 में दो भाषाएँ (एक भारतीय) निर्धारित करती है। कथन 3 NCF-FS 2022 का वर्णन है; NCF-SE पूरे 5+3+3+4 स्कूली चरण को कवर करती है।

mcqs.q_en: PARAKH, the National Assessment Centre envisaged in NEP 2020, has been set up as a unit of:
mcqs.q_hi: NEP 2020 में परिकल्पित राष्ट्रीय आकलन केंद्र PARAKH को किस संस्था की इकाई के रूप में स्थापित किया गया है?
options_en: National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)
options_hi: राष्ट्रीय शैक्षिक अनुसंधान और प्रशिक्षण परिषद (NCERT)
mcqs.explain_en: PARAKH (Performance Assessment, Review and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development) was set up in NCERT in February 2023; it ran the Rashtriya Sarvekshan on 4 Dec 2024 in Classes 3, 6 and 9. NTA conducts entrance tests, not school assessment.
mcqs.explain_hi: PARAKH (Performance Assessment, Review and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development) की स्थापना फरवरी 2023 में NCERT में हुई; इसने 4 दिसंबर 2024 को कक्षा 3, 6 और 9 में राष्ट्रीय सर्वेक्षण किया। NTA प्रवेश परीक्षाएँ कराती है, स्कूली आकलन नहीं।

mcqs.q_en: The National Curriculum Framework for School Education 2023 was developed by which body, and who chaired the National Steering Committee that guided it?
mcqs.q_hi: स्कूली शिक्षा के लिए राष्ट्रीय पाठ्यचर्या की रूपरेखा 2023 किस संस्था ने विकसित की और इसके मार्गदर्शन हेतु गठित राष्ट्रीय संचालन समिति के अध्यक्ष कौन थे?
mcqs.explain_en: NCERT prepared NCF-FS 2022 and NCF-SE 2023 under the National Steering Committee chaired by Dr K. Kasturirangan, who also chaired the NEP drafting committee. Yash Pal chaired NCF 2005; Subramanian chaired the 2016 policy committee.
mcqs.explain_hi: NCERT ने डॉ. के. कस्तूरीरंगन की अध्यक्षता वाली राष्ट्रीय संचालन समिति के अधीन NCF-FS 2022 और NCF-SE 2023 तैयार कीं; वे NEP मसौदा समिति के भी अध्यक्ष थे। यशपाल NCF 2005 से और सुब्रमण्यन 2016 की नीति समिति से जुड़े थे।
mcqs.source: NCF-SE 2023 foreword (NCERT); MoE constitution of National Steering Committee, Sept 2021

mcqs.q_en:
Assertion (A): NEP 2020 provides for census examinations in Grades 3, 5 and 8 to track learning outcomes.
Reason (R): NEP 2020 abolished the Grade 10 and Grade 12 board examinations.
mcqs.q_hi:
अभिकथन (A): NEP 2020 अधिगम परिणामों पर नज़र रखने के लिए कक्षा 3, 5 और 8 में जनगणना (census) परीक्षाओं का प्रावधान करती है।
कारण (R): NEP 2020 ने कक्षा 10 और कक्षा 12 की बोर्ड परीक्षाएँ समाप्त कर दीं।
options_en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
options_hi: A और R दोनों सत्य हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या है
A और R दोनों सत्य हैं परंतु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है
A सत्य है परंतु R असत्य है
A असत्य है परंतु R सत्य है
mcqs.explain_en: NEP 2020 keeps board exams for Grades 10 and 12, makes them competency based and allows them up to twice a year; it adds State census exams in Grades 3, 5 and 8. So A is true and R is false.
mcqs.explain_hi: NEP 2020 कक्षा 10 और 12 की बोर्ड परीक्षाएँ बनाए रखती है, उन्हें दक्षता-आधारित बनाती है और वर्ष में दो बार तक देने की अनुमति देती है; साथ ही कक्षा 3, 5 और 8 में राज्य स्तरीय जनगणना परीक्षाएँ जोड़ती है। अतः A सत्य और R असत्य है।

mcqs.q_en: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
mcqs.q_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा युग्म सही सुमेलित है?
options_en: Vidya Pravesh – three-month play-based school preparation module for Grade 1
Balvatika – remedial programme for Grade 8 students
Jadui Pitara – credit bank for higher education
NISHTHA – scholarship scheme for meritorious students
options_hi: विद्या प्रवेश – कक्षा 1 के लिए तीन माह का खेल-आधारित विद्यालय तैयारी मॉड्यूल
बालवाटिका – कक्षा 8 के विद्यार्थियों के लिए उपचारात्मक कार्यक्रम
जादुई पिटारा – उच्च शिक्षा के लिए क्रेडिट बैंक
निष्ठा – मेधावी विद्यार्थियों के लिए छात्रवृत्ति योजना
mcqs.explain_en: Vidya Pravesh is the 12-week school-readiness module for Grade 1 under NIPUN Bharat. Balvatika is the pre-school class before Grade 1, Jadui Pitara is the play-based learning material for ages 3–8, and NISHTHA is the teacher and school-head training programme.
mcqs.explain_hi: विद्या प्रवेश निपुण भारत के अंतर्गत कक्षा 1 के लिए 12-सप्ताह का विद्यालय-तत्परता मॉड्यूल है। बालवाटिका कक्षा 1 से पहले की पूर्व-प्राथमिक कक्षा है, जादुई पिटारा 3–8 वर्ष के लिए खेल-आधारित शिक्षण सामग्री है, और निष्ठा शिक्षकों व विद्यालय प्रमुखों का प्रशिक्षण कार्यक्रम है।
mcqs.source: NCERT Vidya Pravesh Guidelines; NIPUN Bharat Guidelines; NISHTHA (NCERT)

changes: MCQs: I solved all 15 before looking at the keys and every key is correct. Each has exactly one right option, statement-type questions check out line by line, and the Hindi matches the English, including option order. No key changes.

Reading (higher education): the VBSA Bill 2025 was wrongly presented as the legislative form of HECI's four verticals. Per the PRS summary in research/05, it replaces UGC, AICTE and NCTE through three councils (Viniyaman, Gunvatta, Manak) and has no grant-giving power. Added that it went to a JPC on 16 Dec 2025, plus a trap line and an update to Remember #15.
Reading/quick facts/Common traps/Remember #11/Q8 explanation (EN+HI): PM SHRI '14,597 schools' → 'more than 14,500 schools' (the Cabinet figure). 14,597 could not be confirmed.

Reading (PM SHRI): 'first list in 2023 had 6,207 schools' → on 29 July 2023 the PM released the first instalment of funds to 6,207 PM SHRI schools. 6,207 was a funding instalment, not a selection list.

Reading (PM SHRI Delhi angle): removed 'Delhi signed the PM SHRI MoU in 2025'. The knowledge base does not confirm it. Kept what it does support: Delhi stayed out under the earlier government, launched CM SHRI schools in 2025, and opened Heritage Clubs in 75 CM SHRI schools in Sept 2026.
Reading (Section 7 table): UDISE+ 2025-26 'teachers crossed 1 crore for the first time' → about 1.02 crore teachers. The 1-crore mark was first crossed in UDISE+ 2024-25 (Aug 2025).

Reading (Section 7 table): dropped the '70 indicators' count for PGI 2.0. It conflicts with the 73 indicators in PGI 2.0's original design and could not be confirmed. Added Chandigarh's 766 points and its 4th straight year on top.
Reading (NCF-SE): removed the 'Panchaadi five-step pedagogy (Aditi, Bodh, Abhyas, Prayog, Prasar)' line credited to NCF-FS. It could not be traced to NCF-FS or NCF-SE. Panchakosha stays.
Reading (NCF-SE Grades 9–10): removed '16 essential courses over the two years' because it could not be confirmed. The eight curricular areas stay.
Reading (four NCFs table): NCFTE/NCFAE 'In process' (unverifiable status) → the bodies NEP assigns them to: NCTE with NCERT for NCFTE, and a new NCERT constituent body for adult education for NCFAE.

Reading (board exams): reworded the unclear 'CBSE held the first second Class 10 board exam in 2026' as: 2026 was CBSE's first year of two Class 10 board exams (main 17 Feb–11 Mar; second 15–21 May; better score counts), per research/05.
Reading (PARAKH): added that the NEP text calls SQAAF the School Quality Assessment and Accreditation Framework. The NCERT/PARAKH document is titled 'Assessment and Assurance'.

Note: WebSearch was denied this session, so nothing was checked live. I kept 2026 items only where research/05-current-affairs.md supports them: Samagra Shiksha 3.0 not approved, TET deadline 31 Aug 2028, ULLAS 5th/6th States, the NCERT case closed 1 Sep 2026, and VBSA still pending.
